belief.answer: The following finite matrix-rank formula gives the answer for every allowed vector b, without genericity assumptions. Set h=2g−2, N=4g−4, d=2g−1−k, Q=⌊N/k⌋, B=2h+1+dQ and J=B+N+dQ+1. Put φ=∑_{j=0}^{r−1}b_jt^{−(2g−1−2j)}, q=kt^kφ and a=−(1/2)t^{−h}(1−t^{4g+2})^{1/2}. All matrices acting on polynomials in w below are taken modulo w^{N+1}. Let P be the substitution matrix F(u)↦F(tw(1−qw^k)^{−1/k}); explicitly, P_{mn}=t^n(n/k)_j q^j/j! if m=n+jk with j≥0, and P_{mn}=0 otherwise, for 0≤m,n≤N. Let D and C be multiplication by 1−qw^k and −t^{−1}−t^kφ′w^k, respectively. Define T_O=P, T_L=aDP, and T_S=((aP,0),(aCP,DP)) in block notation. Define H_B={s∈Z:0≤s≤B and s even}∪{s∈Z:2g+1≤s≤B and s odd}, and F_s=t^{−s} for even s, F_s=t^{−s}(1−t^{4g+2})^{1/2} for odd s. For each m×m matrix T among T_O,T_L,T_S, form the finite complex matrix M(T) with rows (α,j), 1≤α≤m, 1≤j≤J, columns (i,s), 1≤i≤m, s∈H_B, and entries M(T)_{(α,j),(i,s)}=[t^{−j}](a^{−1}(T^{−𝖳})_{αi}F_s). Then \boxed{\Delta_b=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_S)-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_O)-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_L)}.

Let D and C be multiplication by 1−qw^k and −t^{−1}−t^kφ′w^k, respectively. Define T_O=P, T_L=aDP, and T_S=((aP,0),(aCP,DP)) in block notation. Define H_B={s∈ℤ:0≤s≤B and s even}∪{s∈ℤ:2g+1≤s≤B and s odd}, and F_s=t^{−s} for even s and F_s=t^{−s}(1−t^{4g+2})^{1/2} for odd s.
